 Never Satisfied | Revs carry relentless mindset into return to Audi MLS Cup Playoffs
 Emma Moneuse
 Copy URL 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 FOXBOROUGH, Mass. – From the very first day of preseason, head coach Marko Mitrović has helped the New England Revolution build an identity rooted in relentlessness; not just when it comes to winning games, but staying relentlessly consistent, humble, present, and true. That mentality carried the Revolution to a third-place finish in the Eastern Conference, and it has readied them as they prepare for the first match of the postseason campaign.
 The Revs have had a remarkable year thus far – one of the best in club history – finishing with 18 regular season wins, one of the strongest defensive records in the league, 11 home victories, 58 points, and countless moments to make the fans in Foxborough proud.
 Of course, the playoffs are somewhat of a clean slate. They’re high stakes, high pressure, and a place where anything can happen. But for a Revs side that has refused to waver from their identity this season, the approach is no different when it comes to Round One against the Philadelphia Union.
 “This whole season has been step by step. We're building an identity, and I think it's that identity that comes first. That was the foundation we instilled in preseason. Then when we get into big moments like this, it's kind of falling back on what you've trained and what you've built. It's a very exciting part of the year, but it's only building on what we've already built throughout the last 10 months,” explained defender Will Sands.
 Mitrović has said time and again that it’s all about taking it day-by-day; more specifically, taking the right actions every day and maximizing every opportunity. His message has been as consistent as the team’s play, and that isn’t changing now.
 “Champions behave like champions before they become champions. And so, if suddenly you get to playoffs and you're just like ‘Oh, now we're going to change and do something different,’ well, why weren't you doing that the entire time?” said assistant coach Michael Morris. “The willingness to fight in any circumstance is amazing. You can talk about tactics and all types of things, and we definitely try to be as prepared as possible for every match, but if there aren't those core behaviors and that level of competitiveness, that willingness to fight and sometimes even suffer together, sometimes the tactics, they're just not relevant.”
 Earning homefield advantage after their top-four finish, the Revs enter the Round One Best-of-3 series against the Philadelphia Union as hosts in Game 1 at Gillette Stadium on Saturday afternoon. After taking down Philly twice in the regular season, the team feels confident in their understanding of the opponent.
 “We know what to do to beat them. We have a clear plan. Obviously, coming from Marko and his staff, they prepare for every game in the best way. We have a clear idea of what to do. When you are a team that has a clear identity and knows what to do in every moment, you feel very confident,” captain Carles Gil said ahead of Saturday’s match.
 At home this season, the Revs’ 35 points were tied for second-most in MLS. They earned three points against the Union at Gillette Stadium from a 2-1 win back in May, followed up by another 2-1 victory at Subaru Park in October. While the wins provide some confidence, New England know that every game is different.
 The Revolution enter the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs for the first time since 2023, after failing to reach the postseason in the previous two campaigns. While it feels like some time since New England have had the chance to make a run for the Cup, the club is no stranger to postseason play.
 The Revolution are one of seven MLS clubs with more than 50 playoff matches played in their history. All-time, the Revs are 13-5-7 at home in the postseason, outscoring opponents 39-20 in Foxborough. The Revs have made it to the MLS Cup Final five times, yet to get their hands on the Philip F. Anschutz Trophy. With the Mitrović mindset leading the way, it feels like things could be different this time around.
 “I feel like we’re ready for everything because we know what to do in every moment,” said Gil. “We arrive to the playoffs in the right way, after a very good regular season. Now it’s the big moments coming. We have been waiting, this club, since 2023, our last playoffs. So, we’re very excited.”
 Kickoff at Gillette Stadium is set for 2:00 p.m. ET on Saturday, and a season’s worth of belief will be on display in front of the Foxborough Faithful. It's only Game 1, but for a team that has trusted their identity all year, it could be the first step toward something much bigger.
 Emma Moneuse
